title: I-CEM: Context-Aware Evidence Minimization for Privacy-Conscious Harmful-Speech Dataset Release

creators.name: Örene, Batın
creators.affiliation: Department of Computer Engineering, Bahçeşehir University

description:
Code, experiment configs, run manifests, and aggregate results for the WOAH 2026 paper Context-Aware Evidence Minimization for Privacy-Conscious Harmful-Speech Dataset Release.

I-CEM is a deterministic release baseline for sharing harmful-speech corpora. It masks identifier spans, selects evidence tokens by leave-one-out erasure attribution against a frozen classifier, and expands the retained spans only when rule-based target–harm or stance–harm relations fire. Releasing only classifier-important tokens corrupts the data: an independent lexicon-free LLM judge recovers the targeted group from such excerpts only 36% of the time and reads 53% of non-hateful excerpts as hateful. I-CEM's primary result is target recovery, improving from 58% to 67% over a token-matched fixed window, a gain that replicates against gold target labels.

No datasets, raw posts, or transformed release rows are included. The paper is published separately by the ACL and is not distributed here.
